This unconscious adjustment makes connected speech smoother and faster.

quests.explanation: Yod-coalescence occurs between 'did' and 'you': the final consonant /d/+/j/ of 'did' fuses with the initial /j/ of 'you' to produce →/dʒ/. The phrase sounds like 'dijyou'. This is extremely common in everyday English: 'did you' → /dɪdʒuː/, 'last year' → /lɑːstʃɪə/, 'miss you' → /mɪʃuː/.
